links.outcome: Guideline concordance of LLMs versus clinicians of varying expertise on same cases
links.effect: AI correct 91.0% vs professors 82.1%/68.6%/65.7%, specialist 50.0%, residents 32.1%/21.4%; composite 10.3 vs 5.2-9.2/12; AI outperformed all human groups (p<0.01).
links.quote: Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons confirmed that AI models significantly outperformed all human groups (p < 0.01), professors outperformed residents (p < 0.001), and specialists performed better than residents (p < 0.05).

links.outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy versus ESC/EAS guidelines, including LDL-C targets and risk stratification
links.effect: AI correct 91.0% (Claude 94.3%, GPT-4 90.7%, DeepSeek 87.9%); 25 errors, 56% risk miscalculation, 8.0% wrong LDL-C target; DeepSeek weaker in risk assessment (2.3 vs 2.9).
links.quote: AI models achieved guideline compliance in 382 out of 420 responses (91.0%), significantly exceeding all human groups.

links.outcome: Simulated LDL-C target attainment for AI alone, clinicians alone, and combined AI-professor workflow
links.effect: Simulated LDL-C target attainment 83% AI, 64% cardiology professors, and 92% for AI draft plus professor supervision (12 very high-risk patients).
links.quote: Of particular clinical significance, a combined workflow incorporating AI-generated draft recommendations with professor supervision yielded a simulated target attainment rate of 92%, exceeding the performance of any single respondent group and approaching the ideal clinical target of >90% guideline adherence.

links.outcome: AI error patterns in demographic subgroups (elderly female patients)
links.effect: Of 25 AI errors, 14 (56%) were risk miscalculation, eight in elderly female patients where SCORE2-OP was incorrectly applied.
links.quote: Among 25 errors made by AI models, 14 (56.0%) involved risk miscalculation, with eight specifically occurring in elderly female patients where SCORE2-OP was incorrectly applied.
